_comment: Guided tour for the Number & Brightness tool. Steps point at real controls and wait for the user to press them; the demo is a simulated scan with monomers (left) and dimers (right) at the same intensity, so every number can be checked against the truth. Read by chisurf.gui.widgets.tools.guided_tour.

steps.title: What N&B measures
steps.text:
Number & Brightness reads the size of the photon packets from how much each pixel's intensity fluctuates from frame to frame. A few bright molecules and many dim ones can give the same intensity — they do not give the same fluctuations.

Per pixel: apparent brightness B = σ²/⟨k⟩, molecular brightness ε = B − 1 (the −1 removes shot noise) and molecule number n = ⟨k⟩/ε. A dimer is twice as bright as its monomer, which is what makes oligomerisation visible.

Eight steps; you press the buttons.

steps.title: Start with data whose answer is known
steps.text: The demo is a simulated confocal scan written as an ordinary PTU file: monomers (ε = 0.5 counts per dwell, n = 6) on the left half, dimers (ε = 1.0, n = 3) on the right. Both halves have the same mean intensity.

await.hint: Press 🧪 Load demo. It writes the file once and runs the analysis.

steps.title: The intensity cannot tell them apart
steps.text: The two halves are equally bright on average — an intensity image shows one uniform square. Keep that in mind for the next map.

steps.title: The brightness can
steps.text:
ε is about 0.5 on the left and 1.0 on the right: the factor of two of a dimer. The number map shows the mirror image (6 versus 3).

Each pixel's value is noisy — the precision grows with the number of frames — so read populations, not single pixels.

steps.title: Pick a population on the parameter plane
steps.text:
The plane is a 2-D histogram of every pixel, intensity horizontally and B vertically. The two species sit at B ≈ 1.5 and B ≈ 2.0 at the same intensity.

Draw a rectangle over the upper cloud with the rectangle button of Gate regions.

steps.title: …and see where it is in the image
steps.text: Gated pixels shows the intensity of the pixels inside the gate. Gating the bright cloud lights up the right half: the dimers, found from brightness alone. The status box lists how many pixels were picked and their median ε and n.

steps.title: Real data needs corrections first
steps.text: Anything else that fluctuates adds to σ² and masquerades as brightness. Detrend segments removes photobleaching (and keeps each pixel's mean, which B divides by); Subtract / Add back remove immobile structure and slow drifts. Set them before you trust ε.

steps.title: Know your detector
steps.text: The −1 in ε = B − 1 is only right for a photon-counting detector. An analog detector (PMT in current mode, camera) has a gain S and an offset: image a static intensity gradient, run, and press 📐 Calibrate analog to read them from the variance-versus-mean line. Dead time shrinks the variance of bright pixels and needs the pixel dwell.
